title: Sources, locations and updates
text:
What this edition contains
The annual workflow is selected directly from the existing canonical guide. The incremental-model plan is selected directly from its existing canonical page. There are no independently edited public Quarto copies or downloadable scientific datasets. The internal working website remains available under its existing access controls.
No observational data files are used to build this edition. Years in the model plan are intended input endpoints, not certification of delivery, acceptance or completed model runs. The workflow source was inspected on 9 October 2026; the incremental sequence records instructions supplied on 14 October 2026. These content dates are separate from the build time below.

title: Sources, locations and updates
text:
Reproduce and update this publication

Edit methodological text in its canonical source. For the imported annual guide, edit in the owning project and refresh its canonical saved guide; keep that source relationship recorded.
Review changes to the selected sections and update their exact hashes in public/allowlist.json only after confirming that the public text remains within the approved methodological scope. Unselected text and files are not copied.
Run python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_public_wiki.py". Preview with python3 scripts/build_public_wiki.py --preview --output-dir /tmp/pollock-public-preview-NEW. Preview output cannot pass a release validation.
Commit the reviewed source and build changes. From a clean canonical checkout, run python3 scripts/build_public_wiki.py --output-dir /tmp/pollock-public-release-NEW, then python3 scripts/public_release.py /tmp/pollock-public-release-NEW.
Use existing authorized account access to publish the exact generated file set to the public output repository. Do not copy the private repository history or the complete internal website. Check the previous output inventory before replacing files; stop on unrelated files or unexpected differences.
Verify the public deployment and all four page URLs anonymously. Confirm that navigation, search and sitemap contain each document once, that inventory hashes match, and that the internal edition retains its existing access controls.

The build requires Quarto 1.10.18, Python 3.10 or later, and the canonical requirements.txt. It uses a fresh staging directory, copies only approved text selections, and regenerates navigation, search and sitemap. The publication validator rejects unexpected files, altered inventory hashes, duplicate pages, broken local links, local machine paths, and known excluded-payload identifiers. Changed selected text requires renewed review and an updated selection hash.
The source repository and internal website links are labeled restricted because they require GitHub/NOAA access. Those links identify ownership; they do not make restricted content public. This publication uses the public URL as its reading address, while the existing private URL continues to serve the internal edition.

title: Annual EBS pollock assessment workflow
text: Use the prior accepted assessment and its archived run as the starting point. AY means assessment year and AY-1 means the previous year. This public selection describes procedures; it does not report current delivery status or assessment results. The 2026 incremental model plan records the proposed update order, with provisional BTS steps.

title: Annual EBS pollock assessment workflow
text:
Steps to do the assessment

Freeze the starting point. Archive the prior accepted input files, model source and executable, controls, parameter file, report, and projection outputs. Reproduce that run before extending the terminal year. Record objective value, key trajectories, reference points, and the comparison tolerance.
Create an annual run directory. Copy the accepted configuration into a separate AY workspace. Resolve every path in pm.dat, including shared data and control files. Keep the previous accepted run intact.
Start a data delivery register. For each product, record provider, release date, revision, years, spatial coverage, ages, units, checksum, processing script, output file, and status. Distinguish received, checked, incorporated, and accepted.
Update fishery inputs. Reconcile final AY-1 catch, estimate full-year AY catch, and prepare AY-1 catch-at-age, weight-at-age, and composition sample sizes from the EBS sampler. Retain current-year lengths for diagnostics or the accepted terminal-length option.
Update BTS products together. Obtain the bottom-trawl survey index, its matching covariance, age composition, weight-at-age, and sample-size information. Record the estimator and EBS/NBS footprint for each product.
Update ATS and AVO products. Incorporate released summer acoustic-trawl survey products and the acoustic vessel-of-opportunity index. Identify preliminary ages, proxy age-length keys, and missing age deliveries explicitly.
Prepare annual biological schedules. Fit the accepted weight-at-age model after its required fishery and survey inputs pass checks. Update fishery and spawning schedules and retain the accepted maturity, natural mortality, timing, and ageing-error settings unless a reviewed change is specified.
Fit an incremental model sequence. Add catch and fishery inputs first, then survey indices and compositions in separate documented steps. Compare changes in spawning biomass, recruitment, fishing mortality, selectivity, likelihood contributions, and uncertainty.
Finalize and diagnose the assessment. Check compilation logs, exit codes, gradients, Hessian, bounds, residuals, retrospective peels, alternative starts, and required sensitivities. Archive the final fit before preparing projections.
Run harvest projections. Transfer the final population state and biological schedules to SPM/spmR. Update projection years and catch assumptions, then verify the first-year population accounting and the ABC/OFL tables.
Build the SAFE and review package. Generate tables and figures from saved outputs, update review responses and ecosystem material, render in a clean session, and reconcile every management value with the saved assessment and projection files.
Archive the annual release. Retain source snapshots, transformation code, input and output checksums, software versions, seeds, diagnostics, report source, rendered files, and review decisions. Record the final approved advice separately from model-generated maximum values.

title: Annual EBS pollock assessment workflow
section: Building and checking the assessment model
text:
Building and checking the assessment model

Fit and preserve the diagnostics
From a copied annual run directory with a verified pm executable and resolved inputs, the historical command is:
./pm -nox -iprint 150 > fit.log 2>&1
Record the command, executable checksum, start file, source/compiler versions, and process exit code. Retain fit.log, pm.par, pm.rep, pm.std, pm.cor, and the gradient/Hessian products written by that build. Some historical make mpd targets remove log, gradient, and admodel.* files after fitting; review the target or use the direct command so diagnostics remain available.
Require a maximum absolute gradient below 1e-4, a positive-definite Hessian, finite uncertainty, and interpretable parameter estimates. Log compiler warnings and resolve them before recording a clean compilation check. A successful exit code establishes execution; the saved diagnostics establish numerical behavior.


Retrospectives and sensitivities
Use terminal-year-consistent peels. Remove observations according to the availability of each stream at that terminal year, including the fishery age lag, acoustic survey schedule, and missing survey years. Truncate the BTS covariance to the same remaining years and extend or truncate biological and selectivity inputs consistently. Recalculate projection schedules for each peel when comparing advice.

title: Annual EBS pollock assessment workflow
text:
Reference points and harvest projections

Harvest recommendation table
Prepare a machine-readable table of advice year, summary biomass and its age definition, spawning biomass, B0/B40%/B35% where required, FABC, FOFL, maximum permissible ABC, recommended ABC, OFL, catch assumptions, and tier. Select values by named output variable, alternative, and year. Verify those selections against the configuration rather than transferring alternative numbers from another stock’s guide.
Generate the AY+1 and AY+2 tables and any decision table of alternative catches from the same saved projection. Check rounding only after the full-precision comparison. Update the risk table and explain any reduction from maximum permissible ABC using the current assessment and ecosystem evidence.

title: Annual EBS pollock assessment workflow
section: SAFE chapter ecosystem material and annual archive
text:
SAFE chapter ecosystem material and annual archive
Update the executive summary, input changes, methods changes, results, diagnostics, reference points, projections, risk table, and responses to review comments from the final run. Retain previous-assessment values in a separate comparison table. Describe the estimator and spatial coverage for each survey and identify preliminary products in the data section.
Render the complete report in an independent clean R session. Check warnings, citations, cross-references, figure descriptions, table units, years, captions, headings, and the final harvest recommendation table. Inspect the Word/PDF layout and retain the agency’s accessibility checks. Keep editable tables as tables and verify figures at their displayed size.
Archive the input and result manifests, source revisions, software environment, build commands, seeds, model diagnostics, report source, rendered review package, final approved chapter, SARA submission products where required, and review decision record. Before committing a selected release bundle, scan code for credentials and internal database connection details. Keep restricted source data within their authorized storage and record how an authorized analyst can obtain them.

title: 2026 cumulative data-update models
text: This sequence records Jim’s intended incremental data updates for the 2026 EBS pollock assessment. Every model inherits all changes from its predecessor. Model 0 is the baseline with data through 2024; model 0.8 is the end of the proposed updated-data sequence. The model endpoint becomes 2026 at model 0.1 and remains 2026 for all subsequent models. Observation years still differ among data streams.

title: 2026 cumulative data-update models
text:
Keep the endpoints distinct
The 2026 model endpoint does not imply that every observation stream reaches 2026. In this sequence, fishery catch-at-age reaches 2025 and fishery weight-at-age is replaced through 2024. No 2026 fishery age observations are added at model 0.4 or in the downstream steps. BTS weights are first replaced through 2024 at 0.2, then provisionally extended through 2026 at 0.5. The BTS age compositions, index, and covariance are provisionally extended together at 0.6.

title: 2026 cumulative data-update models
text:
Compare and retain the evidence
Use adjacent-model comparisons to describe each new update conditional on the earlier changes. Compare each updated model with model 0 to describe the cumulative change. These differences depend on the update order; they do not establish an order-independent contribution for each data stream. Keep the 0.1 endpoint extension visible in comparisons with the baseline, and compare common historical years separately from the new terminal years.
For each run, retain the input filenames and hashes, source delivery and coverage dates, model endpoint, inherited control settings, executable or code revision, and any preliminary-data qualifications. Once fits are available, record convergence diagnostics and compare spawning biomass, recruitment, fishing mortality, fit to observations, and any derived reference points or projections using matched definitions. Follow the annual model checks and projection handoff. Results remain to be evaluated.

title: 2026 cumulative data-update models
text:
Source and open decision
This page records Jim’s cumulative model-update instructions supplied on 14 October 2026. It documents the planned sequence, rather than an inventory of verified model input files or fitted runs. Confirm the 0.5/0.6 BTS split and downstream numbering before finalizing run labels. Scientific inputs and run acceptance remain with the owning assessment project.
